scope: Local implementation of slice S3a of docs/QR_2_PORTFOLIO_PERFORMANCE_CONTRACT.md (RC-Q28 to RC-Q34) for PM-1 row F10-01: the owner-scoped per-Bot GET /api/paper-performance route (src/postgres/qr2-routes.js), a pure response composer (src/portfolio/qr2-response.js) and an after-commit hook in the request dispatcher. Phase 1 checks the session, own:read, parameters, Bot scope, bounds and an admin step-up inside the request transaction and writes the admin audit row; phase 2 runs the S2 reader after COMMIT in its own REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY transaction. The route is behind QR2_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED, off by default, and is not enabled anywhere.
method: An architecture auditor (Opus 5.5) wrote the S3 design and root accepted it (RC-Q28 to RC-Q33). A coder (Sonnet 5.5) wrote S3a. An independent architecture auditor (Opus 5.5) and a second-opinion reviewer (Fable 5.1) reviewed security, scoping and the hook; both rated it acceptable with minor findings. Two narrow fix rounds followed (history limit from UTC midnight, audit-before-read and end-to-end hook tests, named-key response copies without global serial ids, exact-case periods, error mapping). An independent tester (Sonnet 5.5) ran the suites, single-edit mutations and the M1 and M2 measurements after each round. Root ruled on every finding. Nobody verified their own work.

result: Throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15: test/postgres/qr2-route-http.test.mjs 21 of 21 and test/postgres/qr2-ssi.test.mjs 8 of 8. Without a database: test/qr2-response.test.js and test/request-dispatch-after-commit.test.js pass, and root reran them with test/request-dispatch.test.js (83 of 83). Regression on the files that load the dispatcher or the server passed (request-dispatch 69, request-limits 10, overview 7, news-windows 18, market-chart-states 3, ai-quota 15, pine-bridge-deployments 6, quant-library-derive 23, qr2-portfolio-performance 111 with 2 todo; PostgreSQL overview-http, owner-isolation-http 13, market-chart-states, db-transaction-closed 7, bot-lifecycle-gates 8, journey-http 9, qr2-reader 27, qr2-reader-facts 9, qr2-audit 5). The SSI tests show a SERIALIZABLE reader makes a concurrent funding request fail with 40001 while the REPEATABLE READ product reader does not.

measurements.M1: Local laptop. 1000 fills (about 3500 to 4000 ledger rows): p95 about 1.5 to 1.6 s, flat or open lots; the highest load reachable under the 5000-row limit (about 1430 flat fills): p95 about 2.4 s. The computation is synchronous, so the event loop is blocked for about the computation time (0.6 to 1.6 s per request at 1000 fills). Above 5000 ledger rows the request is refused in about 30 ms.
measurements.M2: Audit lookup is a filtered scan: about 25 ms at 100k audit rows and about 200 to 340 ms at 1M rows; it runs after the answer is sent.

mutations.round2: 7 of 9 killed; the two survivors were test gaps, closed in round 3.

limits: Not enabled anywhere. RC-Q34: before QR2_PERFORMANCE_ENABLED is turned on in any environment, slice S3b must move the computation off the event loop or bound repeated requests, and the read budget is re-checked.
Every account with a fill reads UNAVAILABLE with LEDGER_RULE_UNREPLAYABLE until the per-environment boundary records exist (OD-Q6, slice S9).
Owner item O-1 (which periods the plan history limit covers) is open; the stricter reading applies.
The per-fill strategy-tag and slippage lists of 8.1 are not returned yet (counts only); they need a later row-capped slice.

rootAcceptance.statement: Root reviewed the design, the agent reports, the measurements, the rulings and the final diff and accepted S3a as local engineering evidence for F10-01. Acceptance changes no PM-1 credit by itself and enables nothing.
